rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God can reverse a person's life stages, restoring him from old age through youth and childhood to semen.
rows.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان، عن الضحاك، قال: سمعته يقول

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda interprets the return as God's ability to resurrect and restore the human after death.
rows.anchor: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers resurrection: the next verse's Day when secrets are tested makes the return a resurrection event, with that Day qualifying when God restores the dead alive as before.
rows.anchor: فكان في إتباعه قوله {إنه على رجعه لقادر} [الطارق: 8] نبأ من أنباء القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī understands the sky as returning with clouds and people's provisions each year.
rows.anchor: ترجع بالغيوم وأرزاق العباد كل عام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites al-Mutanakhil's sword verse as poetic evidence for the Arabic usage of al-rajʿ.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول المتنخل في صفة سيف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the sky's return as clouds containing rain.
rows.anchor: عن خصيف، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains al-rajʿ as rainfall and provision returning each year.
rows.anchor: يعني بالرجع: القطر والرزق كل عام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the sky returns people's provisions every year.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima, when asked about the phrase, says it returns with rain.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رجاء: سئل عنها عكرمة، فقال: رجعت بالمطر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid explains it as clouds that rain and then return with rain.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the sky returns people's provisions each year; without this, people and livestock would perish, and he also glosses it as annual rain.
rows.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets al-rajʿ as rain.
rows.anchor: حدثت عن الحسين، قال: سمعت أبا معاذ

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other interpreters take the sky's return to refer to the sun and moon setting and rising.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: يعني بذلك: أن شمسها وقمرها يغيب ويطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the earth's fissuring as its splitting open for vegetation.
rows.anchor: عن خصيف، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the fissure with vegetation emerging, including its yearly emergence.
rows.anchor: عن خصيف، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the earth splits open to expose what lies beneath it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي رجاء، عن الحسن

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the earth splits open to bring forth provision.
rows.anchor: وسئل عنها عكرمة فقال: هذه تصدع عن الرزق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid compares the fissure to the pass at al-Maʾzim in Minā, excluding valleys and steep banks from the comparison.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، قال مجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the earth splits to produce fruits and plants.
rows.anchor: عن معمر، عن قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd links the fissure to plowing and cites the earth being split so grain, grapes, and fodder grow.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk interprets the earth's fissure as vegetation.
rows.anchor: حدثت عن الحسين، قال: سمعت أبا معاذ

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd reports that after Yamāma's losses, ʿUmar urged collecting the Qur'an; Abū Bakr initially refused because the Prophet had not done so, then accepted the proposal and assigned Zayd.
rows.anchor: عن خارجة بن زيد بن ثابت، عن أبيه زيد قال

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd says he gathered the Qur'an from parchment, shoulder blades, and palm stalks; the single sheet later passed from Abū Bakr to ʿUmar and Ḥafṣa.
rows.anchor: في قطع الآدم، وكسر الأكتاف والعسب فلما هلك أبو بكر

rows.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa warned ʿUthmān after seeing Syrians and Iraqis recite differently in Armenia and accuse each other's readings of unbelief.
rows.anchor: ثم إن حذيفة بن اليمان قدم من غزوة كان غزاها، في مرج أرمينية، فلم يدخل بيته حتى أتى عثمان بن عفان

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān commissioned Zayd and the eloquent Abān ibn Saʿīd to produce a codex, write what they agreed on, and refer disagreements to him.
rows.anchor: فأمرني عثمان بن عفان أكتب له مصحفا

words: إن آية ملكه أن يأتيكم التابوت
rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd preferred spelling the word al-tābūt with hāʾ, while Abān preferred tāʾ; ʿUthmān settled the codex spelling as tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقال أبان بن سعيد: التابوت، فرفعنا ذلك إلى عثمان

words: من المؤمنين رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه
rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: While checking the codex, Zayd found the verse about believers fulfilling their covenant with God with Khuzayma ibn Thābit and added it.
rows.anchor: حتى وجدتها عند خزيمة بن ثابت فكتبتها

words: لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم
rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd says the closing verses of al-Tawba were found with another man also called Khuzayma and placed at the sūra's end; he says three verses would have made them a separate sūra.
rows.anchor: حتى وجدتها مع رجل آخر، يدعى خزيمة أيضا، فأثبتها في آخر براءة

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: ʿUthmān borrowed Ḥafṣa's sheet, collated the codex without finding differences, returned it, ordered copies made, then after her death reclaimed and erased the sheet.
rows.anchor: ثم أرسل عثمان إلى حفصة يسألها أن تعطيه الصحيفة، وحلف لها ليردنها إليها

words: ٱدْعُوهُمْ لِءَابَآئِهِمْ هُوَ أَقْسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī uses the rule to call people by their fathers' names as an analogy: lineage is exclusive, whereas language use can belong to multiple peoples.
rows.anchor: لقول الله تعالى ذكره: {ادعوهم لآبائهم هو أقسط عند الله}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads 'from every tongue' to mean that a word shared in form and meaning by Arabic and other peoples belongs to each language, without one having exclusive claim.
rows.anchor: فيه من كل لسان، اتفق فيه لفظ العرب ولفظ غيرها من الأمم التي تنطق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A region between plain and mountain, or land and sea, can truthfully be described by both qualities; naming one does not cancel the other, just as a word can belong to two languages.
rows.anchor: كما لو أن أرضا بين سهل وجبل، لها هواء السهل وهواء الجبل، أو بين بر وبحر، لها هواء البر وهواء البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects the claim that 'from every tongue' means some Qur'anic expressions are non-Arabic and cannot properly be ascribed to Arabic, since God calls the Qur'an Arabic.
rows.anchor: فبين إذا خطأ قول من زعم أن القائل من السلف: في القرآن من كل لسان، إنما عنى بقيله ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges the theory that foreign peoples' terms were borrowed into Arabic: the reverse, Arabic terms spreading to other peoples, is equally possible, and the opponent must supply proof distinguishing them.
rows.anchor: ما برهانك على صحة ما قلت في ذلك من الوجه الذي يجب التسليم له؟ فقد علمت من خالفك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues the community could transmit some of the seven modes and omit the rest; they fulfilled their duty, and preserving every mode could have harmed Islam and its people.
rows.anchor: وفي تركهم نقل ذلك كذلك أوضح الدليل على أنهم كانوا في القراءة بها مخيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Differences of case ending, vowel, consonant movement, or letter form with the same written outline are unrelated to the seven-aḥruf report, since disputing such variants is not disbelief.
rows.anchor: فأما ما كان من اختلاف القراءة، في رفع حرف وجره ونصبه، وتسكين حرف وتحريكه ونقل حرف إلى آخر، مع اتفاق الصورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no need to identify the six other dialects: even if known, they are no longer recited today.
rows.anchor: أما الألسن الستة التي قد نزلت القراءة بها، فلا حاجة بنا إلى معرفتها، لأنا لو عرفناها، لم نقرأ اليوم بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report attributed to Ibn ʿAbbās assigns five modes to the ʿajuz of Hawāzin and two to Quraysh and Khuzāʿa, but al-Ṭabarī rejects its chains as proof: al-Kalbī/Abū Ṣāliḥ and Qatāda, who never met Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن خمسة منها لعجز هوازن، واثنين منها لقريش وخزاعة. وروي جميع ذلك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says revelation has four names in Arabic—Qur'an, Furqān, Kitāb, and Dhikr—and each has a distinct meaning and usage.
rows.anchor: سمى تنزيله الذي أنزله على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أسماء أربعة: منهن القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses 'when We recite it' as 'We made it clear' and 'follow its recitation' as 'act according to it.'
rows.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس، في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers Ibn ʿAbbās's derivation of Qur'an from reciting or reading; he understands the report to mean act on what was clarified through recitation.
rows.anchor: والواجب أن يكون تأويله على قول ابن عباس، من التلاوة والقراءة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbās report says God undertakes to make the Prophet recite without forgetting; when it is recited to him, he should follow its contents.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: On Qatāda's account, Qur'an is a verbal noun meaning gathering and joining parts together, as in saying a she-camel has not gathered a fetus.
rows.anchor: على قول قتادة، فإن الواجب أن يكون مصدرا، من قول القائل قرأت الشيء إذا جمعته وضممت بعضه إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī cites ʿAmr ibn Kulthūm's poem using Qur'an to mean recitation, supporting Ibn ʿAbbās's derivation from reading.
rows.anchor: يعني به قائله: تسبيحا وقراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He answers that Qur'an may name recitation though the text is recited, just as kitāb can name a written object through the act of writing.
rows.anchor: قيل كما جاز أن يسمى المكتوب كتابا، بمعنى كتاب الكاتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's divorce verse calls the written divorce document a kitāb, illustrating that a written object may take the name of the act that produced it.
rows.anchor: في صفة كتاب طلاق، كتبه لامرأته

rows.speaker: عكرمة، السدي، وجماعة غيرهما
rows.claim: Ikrima, al-Suddī, and other scholars explain Furqān as deliverance or salvation.
rows.anchor: عن عكرمة، أنه كان يقول: «هو النجاة»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets Furqān as a way out or deliverance.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن عباس يقول: الفرقان: المخرج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid glosses Furqān as a way out and says the Day of Furqān is the day God distinguished truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reconciles the reported glosses: an exit is salvation, salvation brings victory over an aggressor, and that victory separates a person from the wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: من جعل له مخرج من أمر كان فيه فقد جعل ذلك المخرج منه نجاة، وكذلك إذا نجى منه فقد نصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He derives Furqān from separating two things; the Qur'an separates right from wrong through proofs, laws, rulings, and by aiding the truthful and defeating the false claimant.
rows.anchor: وأصل الفرقان عندنا: الفرق بين الشيئين، والفصل بينهما وقد يكون ذلك بقضاء، واستنقاذ، وإظهار حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāb is a verbal noun from writing, like qiyām from standing and ḥisāb from reckoning; it denotes the writer's joined or separate letters, though the Qur'an itself is written.
rows.anchor: وأما تأويل اسمه الذي هو الكتاب فهو مصدر من قولك كتبت كتابا، كما تقول قمت قياما، وحسبت الشيء حسابا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Adhāt Banī Ghifār, Gabriel successively conveyed commands to recite on one, two, three, then seven aḥruf; the Prophet sought relief for his community, and said any of the seven is correct.
rows.anchor: أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، كان عند أضاة بني غفار

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy heard two men recite Sūrat al-Naḥl differently; each said the Prophet had taught him his reading.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، أنه قال: سمعت رجلا، يقرأ في سورة النحل قراءة تخالف قراءتي، ثم سمعت آخر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet asked each man to recite and affirmed both readings as good, calming Ubayy's distress at the differences.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأحدهما: «اقرأ»

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When Ubayy reddened with demonic misgivings, the Prophet touched his chest and prayed for Satan to be driven away from him.
rows.anchor: فعرف ذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في وجهي، فضرب بيده في صدري

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God granted seven aḥruf and a request with each successive command; he asked forgiveness for his community and reserved his third intercession for Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: فقال: إن الله يأمرك أن تقرأ القرآن على سبعة أحرف، ولك بكل ردة مسألة
